passage:
Yogesh had stopped opening the banking app. Two months earlier a colleague's hot tip had swallowed most of his emergency savings, and each time the balance flashed he felt stupid enough to want to vanish. At home he changed the subject whenever his parents asked about money.

On Sunday his friend Dhruv found him staring at a spreadsheet he had built and deleted twice. "You look terrible."

After a long pause Yogesh told him everything. Dhruv didn't laugh. "People lose money on tips all the time. Can we write down what happened?"

They made a list: bought after one message, no research, put in more to win it back. Yogesh set two rules: never put in money he couldn't afford to lose, and never act on someone else's excitement. Then he opened the app, started a small monthly transfer, and rang his mother.

qa.q: What two rules did Yogesh set?
qa.a: Yogesh set two rules: never put in money he couldn't afford to lose, and never act on someone else's excitement.

qa.q: Why had Yogesh stopped opening the banking app?
qa.a: Each time the balance flashed he felt stupid enough to want to vanish, so avoiding the app was a way of hiding the shame.

qa.q: What would you advise Yogesh to do now that he has told Dhruv?
qa.a: Keep reviewing what happened, stick to the rules, rebuild slowly with the small monthly transfer, and keep his family in the picture.

qa.q: How does Dhruv see Yogesh's loss?
qa.a: Dhruv treats it as a common experience rather than something to laugh at, and helps Yogesh look at what happened calmly.

grounding: Yogesh loses savings on a hot tip, feels stupid and hides it, then stops, reviews, tells someone and rebuilds slowly with rules.

passage:
"Ankita, you've been quiet all week. What's wrong?"
"Nothing, Sumit bhaiya."
"You haven't eaten your dinner."
Ankita pushed her plate away. "I lost my savings. All of it. Someone in my office group said a small company's share would triple. I put everything in. It crashed."
Sumit sat down beside her. "How much?"
"Enough. I feel so stupid. I didn't tell anyone for three weeks."
"You're not stupid. Lots of people lose money on tips. What's stupid is hiding it and trying again to win it back."
"I was thinking about that, honestly."
"Don't. First, stop. Then let's write down what happened: who gave the tip, what you checked, what you didn't."
"And then?"
"Then we rebuild. Slowly. Sit with a proper adviser before investing anything again. Can I tell Maa?"
Ankita wiped her eyes and nodded. "Tomorrow. Together."

qa.q: How long had Ankita kept the loss to herself?
What was Ankita feeling about the loss?
qa.a: She felt stupid and ashamed, hiding it for three weeks and even thinking of trying again to win it back.
Stopping, writing down what happened, rebuilding slowly with a proper adviser, and telling Maa together.

qa.q: How might Sumit bhaiya see Ankita's silence?
qa.a: He was worried by her quietness and not eating, and sees the hiding as more dangerous than the loss itself.

grounding: After losing savings on a hot tip the protagonist feels stupid and hides it; a brother helps her stop, review what happened, tell family and rebuild slowly.

passage:
I'm Simran, and last year I lost most of my savings on a tip from a trading group. A stranger posted charts, people cheered, and I put in two years of savings in one afternoon. Two weeks later it was worth almost nothing.
Looking back, the loss wasn't the worst part. The hiding was. I told my flatmate Urmila I was "just tired". I kept checking the app at night, thinking about putting in more to win it back.
Then one night Urmila found me crying in the kitchen and made me talk. She didn't lecture. She said, "My uncle did the same. It happens to lots of people." That helped.
We wrote down what happened: who gave the tip, what I didn't check, why I rushed. I left the trading group. I met a registered adviser. Now I save a fixed amount each month, and I don't invest in anything I can't explain to Urmila in two sentences.

qa.q: How much did Simran put in that afternoon?
qa.a: Two years of savings, in one afternoon.

qa.q: What was Simran feeling while hiding the loss?
qa.a: Simran felt ashamed and trapped, pretending to be tired and tempted to put in more to win it back.

qa.q: How did Simran begin to rebuild?
qa.a: By telling Urmila, writing down what happened, leaving the group, meeting a registered adviser, and saving steadily with simple rules.

qa.q: How might Urmila have felt finding Simran crying in the kitchen?
qa.a: Urmila was probably worried and caring, and chose comfort over a lecture so Simran could open up.

grounding: After losing savings on a tip the protagonist hides it in shame, then tells someone, reviews what happened and rebuilds slowly with rules.
